rows.protocolQuote: our Wi-Fi surfing-test employs a display brightness of 150 cd/m 2 and cycles through different websites automatically at 40 second intervals
rows.note: Review dated 09/25/2012 (byline "Felix Sold & Patrick Afschar Kaboli ( translated by Till), 09/25/2012"); capture is from Dec 2013.

Byline "Michael Moser ( translated by A Kammel), 10/24/2013". Reviewer flags the result as likely too low: "Our Wi-Fi browsing test crashed repeatedly on both our test device and the iPhone 5 when opening a certain website ... we had to reopen the browser app every 5 minutes ... the resulting 10 hours are probably too conservative a value". No brightness stated in this review.

Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Review-Apple-iPhone-5c-Smartphone.103537.0.html (Wayback 429). "Veröffentlicht am 04.10.2013". No brightness stated in the battery section.

rows.protocolQuote: Eine bessere Vergleichbarkeit liefern die Tests mit angepasster Display-Helligkeit von 150 cd/m². Im Test „ Surfen über WLAN “ wird, bei lediglich aktivierter Wifi-Verbindung, ein Browserskript ausgeführt, welches alle 40 Sekunden eine andere Webseite aufruft.
rows.note: Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-6-Smartphone-Review.127057.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 25.09.2014". Value was updated after iOS 8.0.2 (+79 min per the page's update note); the printed value is the updated one.

rows.protocolQuote: Bei den Tests mit angepasster Displayleuchtkraft (150 cd/m²) ist die Laufzeit im Test „Surfen über WLAN“ überraschend höher als bei der Videowiedergabe.
rows.note: Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-6-Plus-Smartphone-Review.127258.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 02.10.2014".

Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-6S-Smartphone-Review.151403.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 30.09.2015". Battery section does not restate the brightness.

rows.protocolQuote: In beiden Fällen dimmen wir die Helligkeit auf 150 cd/m 2 und deaktivieren alle Kommunikationsmodule – bis auf WLAN beim Surftest. Dabei ruft der Browser alle 30 Sekunden eine neue Webseite auf
rows.note: Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-6S-Plus-Smartphone-Review.151376.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 30.09.2015".

rows.protocolQuote: Beim WLAN-Surfen mit 150 cd/m 2 Helligkeit und nur mit WLAN als aktives Funkmodul kommt das Apple iPhone 7 auf sehr gute 8 Stunden und 37 Minuten.
rows.note: Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-7-Smartphone-Review.173851.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 18.09.2016".

Source is the German edition (notebookcheck.com) of the review; English edition: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Apple-iPhone-7-Plus-Smartphone-Review.173844.0.html. "Veröffentlicht am 18.09.2016". Battery section does not restate the brightness.

rows.quote: WiFi continues to take the cake at 6 hours and 40 minutes of total usage
rows.protocolQuote: Each page was loaded by the browser and was set to forward to the next page (in the above order) after 10 seconds; the iPhone’s brightness was set to approximately 50%.
rows.note: Brightness stated as "approximately 50%", not in nits. Byline "by Anand Lal Shimpi on 7/16/2008".

rows.quote: Apple claims that web browsing on WiFi should last you about 9 hours on the new iPhone 3GS; mine lasted 8.83 hours.
rows.note: Understanding the iPhone 3GS, "by Anand Lal Shimpi on July 7, 2009". This page states no brightness or page interval.
